haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes a timer swaps in changed versions, no restart. On read failure it keeps the last good value and retries next tick.

haiku-low.q5: Engineers cannot read prod values. The pod identity orders-api-prod reads prod. The security on-call group writes, via the store CLI under their own identity.
haiku-low.q6: Old keys remain in git history and are treated as leaked. They become harmless only when revoked at the provider, after every pod has switched.
haiku-low.q7: Clients call secrets.get(name) when building each call's Authorization header, reading the current value once per call.
haiku-low.q8: Manually: each pod's latest refresh version ids match the store's current versions, no refresh alert is open, and the old key shows no recent use.
haiku-low.q9: Store access; issue and store new keys; code change switching to store and removing yaml keys (one PR); revoke old provider keys.
haiku-low.q10: Fixed fake keys from config/app.local.yaml's local_secrets section, with no store call. Optional sandbox mode reads orders-api/dev under the developer's own identity.
haiku-low.q11: Treats it as a failed attempt: retries all three reads, up to 4 attempts, then logs the error without values and exits non-zero.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded at process start, before it takes traffic. /healthz returns 503 until all three secrets are loaded, then 200, so the pod is ready only after keys load.
sonnet.q2: It retries (4 attempts, 3 s timeout, 2 s waits, about 18 s worst case), then logs the error and exits non-zero. It never turns ready, so the rollout halts and the old pods keep serving traffic. The platform is expected to restart it.
sonnet.q3: A background timer every 5 minutes reads the latest version of each secret. If the version id differs it swaps in the new value (the old value is kept as previous). If the read fails it keeps the last good value, logs a warning (no values) and retries next tick. After 3 failed cycles in a row (15 min) an alert is raised. Readiness is not affected.
sonnet.q4: Held in process memory in the holder (in the secrets module); a request keeps its header only for its own lifetime. They must never appear on disk, in environment variables or in logs (also not in headers, request objects, exception output or core dumps).
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod service identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Write: the security on-call group, using the store CLI under their own identity. Engineers have no access to prod values.
sonnet.q6: The old keys have been in git history for two years and are treated as leaked, and history is not rewritten. They are made harmless by revoking them at the providers after every pod is confirmed on the new keys.
sonnet.q7: The clients call secrets.get("<name>") on each provider call, when building the Authorization header, instead of copying the key at construction. The value is read once per call.
sonnet.q8: By hand, per key, recorded in the ticket: list the pods in the cluster (exactly the expected pods, all on the migration image or later), read each pod's latest refresh log line and compare its version ids to the store's current versions (via the store CLI), confirm no refresh alert is open, and where the provider shows last use, confirm the old key has not been used since the final pod switched. The security on-call engineer must sign off.
sonnet.q9: 1) Create store paths and access rules (and test them). 2) Issue new keys at providers (old stay active), test them, and write them to the store. 3) Code change in one PR that switches the app to the store, removes the api_key lines from the committed config and adds the guards. 4) Merge and rolling deploy. 5) Verify and soak. 6) Block old images and look for other users of the old keys. 7) Confirm every instance, then revoke the old keys. 8) Close out.
sonnet.q10: With APP_ENV=local (make run), from the local_secrets section of config/app.local.yaml: fixed fake keys, with stub servers and no store call, so no credentials are needed. Optionally make run-sandbox (APP_ENV=dev) reads orders-api/dev/* under the developer's own identity and uses provider sandbox keys.
sonnet.q11: One attempt reads all three secrets, and if any read fails (not found is handled like denied) the attempt fails and the next one re-reads all three. After 4 failed attempts it logs the error and exits non-zero, and never turns ready.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Scheduled rotation is an undecided open question for security. The plan picks no cadence.
